A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same noise-trajectory search framework and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Retained material can be matched across appendix renumbering. The animation linked from v2 is outside the supplied evidence.

before.justification: V1 reports original EDM and Stable Diffusion experiments in Tables 1–2, parameter sweeps, computational analyses, and qualitative generations in its appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds larger-sample evaluations, compositional and counting tests, SDXL results, and additional ablations in Appendices F–G.

M1.justification: The core epsilon-greedy Algorithm 1 and MDP-to-bandit formulation are unchanged. Appendix F.5 adds evaluated inference variants that replace Tweedie-based candidate evaluation with direct noisy-latent classification or predictions from a one-step distilled model. These are limited component substitutions rather than a redesign of the search algorithm.

E1.justification: V1's quantitative text-to-image comparisons primarily use ImageNet class-name prompts, alongside some harder qualitative examples. V2 adds systematic subject-action compositional tests and multi-object counting prompts containing 1–6 number/object clauses in F.2–F.3. These substantially expand the evaluated prompt requirements; the larger ImageNet sample and SDXL substitution are separate setting changes.

E2.justification: The original naive sampling, best-of-N, beam search, MCTS, and zero-order search comparisons remain. Tables 8–9 additionally compare Tweedie-based evaluation against a learned noisy-latent classifier and InstaFlow-based clean-sample prediction. These introduce alternative candidate-evaluation methods, without changing the original search-baseline comparisons.

E3.justification: V2 adds a 300-image EDM evaluation alongside the retained 36-image comparison, detector-based counting and normalized ImageReward evaluations, and an SDXL configuration. Additional protocols vary guidance scale from 1.5 to 12, denoising steps from 18 to 256, and average per-step search iterations. These extend the evaluation design rather than establish reruns or replacements of the original experiments.

E4.justification: F.5 adds ablations testing whether noisy-latent classifiers or distilled predictions improve on Tweedie estimates. G.4 adds guidance-scale and denoising-step sensitivity tests. G.2 expands the adaptive-search-budget proof of concept already present in v1 G.1 into a systematic average-iteration sweep. Existing noise-candidate, iteration, epsilon, and step-size sweeps are retained.

E5.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same standard deviations and explanation that they come from 20 generations per prompt. V2 introduces no new empirical confidence-interval, significance-testing, seed-reporting, or repeated-run procedure. Its additional appendix tables report point estimates without establishing a change to the existing uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: Tables 4–11 and the new Figure 4 substantially expand the reported outcomes; Tables 1–2 remain unchanged. For example, counting rewards are 0.5384 for epsilon-greedy versus 0.4377 for MCTS, and SDXL ImageReward scores are 0.5830 versus 0.5152. These are new-condition comparisons. Table 11 also shows zero-order search slightly exceeding epsilon-greedy on compressibility at T=64 and T=256.

T1.justification: New Appendix D introduces Lipschitz-surrogate and approximation-error assumptions, a truncated noise domain, Theorem 1, and a proof claiming per-step regret bounded by δ + C_d(εNK)^(-1/d), followed by a summed bound across diffusion steps. V1 contains no corresponding regret theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: practical gradient-free noise-trajectory optimization, contextual-bandit-inspired epsilon-greedy search, timestep-dependent exploration, and performance matching or exceeding MCTS, including the same up-to-164% claim.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations defending Tweedie estimates against alternative evaluators, describing a small surrogate-bias floor, and asserting superiority across guidance scales and denoising-step counts. The latter assertion overlooks ties and small zero-order wins in Table 11. Existing discussions of computational cost, population metrics, and reward overoptimization are retained under renamed Appendix J.

D1.justification: The new experiments document compositional and counting prompt templates, object-detection-based count scoring, reward normalization, the noisy-latent classifier, and the InstaFlow-0.9B model used for alternative predictions. Existing pseudocode, main hyperparameters, A100 hardware information, and generation-time disclosures remain unchanged. These are limited additional implementation details.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations for flow-model inference-time scaling, InstaFlow, SDXL, t-SNE, and ImageReward, principally supporting the new appendix material. The main related-work discussion and novelty positioning against Ma et al. and T-SCEND remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative is largely unchanged. V2 adds appendix sections and updates cross-references, adds author email addresses, renames the limitations section to Discussion and Next Steps, and expands the existing future-work bullets into short titled paragraphs. The retained material does not undergo extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: V2 adds eight tables, numbered 4–11, and a new average-search-iteration plot as Figure 4, substantially expanding the experimental displays and rearranging appendix layout. All seven original figure images are retained; several are relocated and renumbered rather than redrawn or replaced.

improvement.justification: The broader prompt evaluations and evaluator ablations address important gaps in v1's empirical support. However, the new regret proof assumes uniform global draws and a nondecreasing pivot, whereas unchanged Algorithm 1 specifies Gaussian draws and replaces the pivot without retaining the incumbent. Table 8 also reports an unexplained beam-search classifier score of 0.9666, versus 0.5536 in retained Table 1. The empirical gains coexist with material new theoretical and reporting problems, preventing a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
